'''Dick Frans Swaab''' (born 17 December 1944) is a [[Dutch people|Dutch]] physician and [[neurobiologist]] (brain researcher).<ref name=GruniadFeb2014>{{cite news|last=Williams|first=Zoe|title=What can Dick Swaab tell us about sex and the brain?|url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2014/jan/28/dick-swaab-sex-brain-theories-men-women-sexuality-womb|newspaper=The Guardian|accessdate=4 February 2014|date=2014-01-28}}</ref> He is a professor of [[neurobiology]] at the [[University of Amsterdam]] and was until 2005 Director of the [[Netherlands Institute for Brain Research]] (Nederlands Instituut voor Hersenonderzoek) of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (Koninklijke Nederlandse Akademie van Wetenschappen).<ref>{{cite web|last1=Spencer|first1=Michael|title=Professor Dick Swaab MD PhD|url=http://www.cosrt.org.uk/latest-news/professor-dick-swaab-md-phd/|website=College of Sexual and Relationship Therapists|accessdate=12 March 2017|date=2016-10-17}}</ref>

==Life==
Swaab graduated at the [[Amsterdams Lyceum]] in 1963. He received his [[doctorate]] of [[medicine]] at the [[University of Amsterdam]] in 1968, and his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in 1970 with professor J. Ariëns Kappers on a [[neuroendocrine]] thesis, and in 1972 he received his [[medical degree]].
He was from 1978 the director of the Netherlands Institute for Brain Research.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last1=Eling|first1=Paul|last2=Hofman|first2=Michel A.|date=2014-04-03|title=The Central Institute for Brain Research in Amsterdam and its Directors|journal=Journal of the History of the Neurosciences|language=en|volume=23|issue=2|pages=109–119|doi=10.1080/0964704X.2013.780810|pmid=24256502|s2cid=43552953|issn=0964-704X}}</ref> In 1979 he was appointed professor of [[neurobiology]] at the University of Amsterdam.
In 1985 he founded the Nederlandse Hersenbank—known in English as The Netherlands Brain Bank<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.brainbank.nl/|title=Welcome to Netherlands Brain Bank|work=Netherlands Brain Bank}}</ref>—to facilitate international research on brain diseases.<ref>{{cite web|title=About the Netherlands Brain Bank|url=http://www.brainbank.nl/about-us/the-nbb/|publisher=Netherlands Brain Bank|accessdate=29 November 2013}}</ref> Swaab is an atheist.<ref>"God bestaat niet" (in Dutch). Positief Atheïsme. 2005-06-07. Archived from the original on 2008-05-11. Retrieved 2008-05-22.“Blasphemy is also a pleasant way of living.”</ref>

==Research==
Swaab is best known for his [[research]] and discoveries in the field of [[brain]] [[anatomy]] and [[physiology]], in particular the impact that various [[hormonal]] and biochemical factors in the [[womb]] have on [[brain development]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://dimasplace.wordpress.com/2011/02/20/brein-en-bewustzijn/ |title=Brein en (bewust)zijn &#124; Dima's Blog |publisher=Dimasplace.wordpress.com |date= 2011-02-20|accessdate=2013-11-29}}</ref> Another area of Swaab's work, which has drawn much attention, is his research on how [[Neuroscience of sex differences|sexual dimorphism]] relates to brain anatomy, as well as research relating to [[Biology and sexual orientation|sexual orientation]] and [[Causes of transsexualism#Biological-based theories|transsexuality]]. Through his years of research, Swaab, according to his own words, came to the [[deterministic]] and [[materialism|materialistic]] conclusion that brains are not things we have, but rather brains are what we are: the physical and chemical processes in our brains determine how we react and who we are.{{citation needed|date=February 2014}} Currently, Swaab is most active in the field of depression and [[Alzheimer's disease|Alzheimer's]] research.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rnw.nl/nederlands/article/hersenonderzoeker-dick-swaab-met-pensioen |title=Announcement &#124; Mededeling &#124; Radio Netherlands Worldwide |publisher=Rnw.nl |date= |accessdate=2013-11-29 |archive-date=2013-04-13 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130413235223/http://www.rnw.nl/nederlands/article/hersenonderzoeker-dick-swaab-met-pensioen |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Swaab's research has on several occasions produced controversy. After conducting research suggesting links between brain anatomy and [[sexual orientation]], Swaab reports receiving death threats from individuals believing this work was attempting to 'pathologize' homosexuality and treat it as a biological abnormality or disorder.<ref>{{cite book|last=Swaab|first=Dick|title=Wij Zijn Ons Brein (We are our brains)|year=2011|page=112}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://theoccasionalbook.com/?p=130|title=We Are Our Brains|website=The Occasional Book|date=8 February 2016 |language=en-US|access-date=2019-05-14}}</ref> Swaab's view that neither free will nor metaphysical entities such as souls or spirits exist has also caused negative reactions among various religious groups.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.deburen.eu/nl/programma/detail/homo-universalis-dick-swaab |title=Homo Universalis: Dick Swaab - Programma - deBuren |publisher=Deburen.eu |date=2007-12-10 |accessdate=2013-11-29 |archive-date=2013-12-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203003924/http://www.deburen.eu/nl/programma/detail/homo-universalis-dick-swaab |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=Jan Willem Nienhuys |url=http://www.skepsis.nl/blog/2011/02/swaab-maakt-gehakt-van-eindeloos-bewustzijn/ |title=Swaab maakt gehakt van Eindeloos Bewustzijn » Skepsis Blog |publisher=Skepsis.nl |date= February 2011|accessdate=2013-11-29|author-link=Jan Willem Nienhuys }}</ref> Swaab consistently defends his studies in the face of such criticism.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.praktijkpsychologiebetgem.nl/actuele-ontwikkelingen/dick-swaab-is-onder-ons-1 |title=Dick Swaab is onder ons (1) &#124; Paul Betgem – Over psychologie, psychiatrie en geestelijke gezondheidszorg |publisher=Praktijkpsychologiebetgem.nl |date=2013-11-22 |accessdate=2013-11-29 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20130413222356/http://www.praktijkpsychologiebetgem.nl/actuele-ontwikkelingen/dick-swaab-is-onder-ons-1 |archivedate=2013-04-13 }}</ref>

==Recognition==
Swaab has numerous scientific awards and was a mentor for at least 84 Ph.D. students, 16 of whom became full professors. He is an editor for several neuroscience journals.<ref name=CV>{{cite web|url=http://www.herseninstituut.knaw.nl/research_groups/swaab_group/team/swaab |title=Swaab: CV |work=knaw.nl |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203034402/http://www.herseninstituut.knaw.nl/research_groups/swaab_group/team/swaab |archivedate=2013-12-03 }}</ref> Swaab has an [[H-index]] of 135, as of 2023, having been cited over 34,000 times.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Scopus preview - Scopus - Author details (Swaab, D. F.)|url=https://www.scopus.com/authid/detail.uri?authorId=35378149600|access-date=2020-07-08|website=www.scopus.com}}</ref>

He is a member, honorary member, and founder of many scientific and professional associations. He was the second person to be awarded the Emil Kraepelin Guest Professorship at the [[Max Planck Institute of Psychiatry]], [[Munich]], Germany, in 1996, and is a visiting professor in three locations in China, and at [[Stanford University]], United States.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scriptum.nl/auteurs/s/dick-swaab |title=Dick Swaab - Scriptum uitgeverij |publisher=Scriptum.nl |date= |accessdate=2013-11-29}}</ref> He also is appointed Chao Kuang Piu Professor at Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, P.-R. China. He has been decorated with the Knight of the [[Order of the Netherlands Lion]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.medicalfacts.nl/2010/10/27/nieuwe-sleutel-om-alzheimer-te-behandelen/ |title=Nieuwe sleutel om Alzheimer te behandelen |publisher=Medicalfacts.nl |date=2010-10-27 |accessdate=2013-11-29}}</ref> a high [[Dutch honours system|order of chivalry]] of the [[Kingdom of the Netherlands]].

==Education==
[[File:DickSwaab1980.jpg|thumb|300x300px|Swaab in 1980.]]
*1963 Final examination [[Amsterdams Lyceum]]
*1968 MD Medicine, [[University of Amsterdam]]
* 1970 Ph.D. Thesis: Factors influencing neurosecretory activity of the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei in rat. A histochemical and cytochemical study. Mentor: Prof. dr. J. Ariëns Kappers
* 1972 General physician, University of Amsterdam

==Professional career==
*Acting director of the Netherlands Institute for Brain Research, an institute of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (KNAW) (1975-1978)
*Director of the [[Netherlands Institute for Brain Research]] (1978-2005)
*Professor of [[neurobiology]] at the medical faculty, University of Amsterdam (1979-2009)
* Leader research team neuropsychiatric disorders, Neth. Inst for Neuroscience (1978-now)
*Founder and, until 2005, director of the Netherlands Brain Bank (1985-2005)

==Workplaces==
* [[Universiteit van Amsterdam|University of Amsterdam]]
* Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience
* Netherlands Brain Bank
* [[Max Planck Institute for Psychiatry]]
* [[Stanford University]]
* Hangzhou, P.-R. China

==Awards and honours==
Swaab has received the following awards and honours:<ref name=CV />
* 'Snoo-van 't Hoogerhuijs' prize (together with Dr. W.J. Honnebier) for work in the field of [[fetal]] [[neuroendocrinology]] (1976)
* 'Hugo van Poelgeest' prize for the Netherlands Brain Bank as an alternative for [[animal experiments]], June 26 (1990)
* Journal of Neural Transmission (36, 195–215, 1975) paper awarded "Citation Classic" status in Current Contents 33, no. 30, p.&nbsp;16. (1990)
* Emil Kraepelin Guest Professorship 1996, Max-Planck-Institut für Psychiatrie, [[Munich]], Germany (1996)
* Royal Honour, “Knight of the [[Order of the Netherlands Lion]]” bestowed by her Royal Highness [[Queen Beatrix of the Netherlands]] (1998)
* Guest Professor of [[Anhui Medical University]], [[Hefei]], [[Anhui]], [[PR China]] (1998/now)
* Guest Professor of [[Capital University of Medical Sciences]], [[Beijing]], [[P.R. China]] (1999/now)
* Federa Prize 2000, Federation of Medical Scientific Societies, November 17, 2000, [[RAI]], Amsterdam, for scientific work in biomedical determinants of Alzheimer's disease (2000)
* GIRES ([[Gender Identity]] Research and Education Society) award 2002 for the article ‘Male-to-Female [[Transsexuals]] Have Female [[Neuron]] Numbers in a [[Limbic]] [[Cell nucleus|Nucleus]].’ (Kruijver et al., J. Clin. Endocrinol. Metabol. 2034-2041 (2002)
* Alzheimer's Association Award: Lifetime Achievement Award in Alzheimer's Disease Research. Received at the 8th International Conference on Alzheimer's Disease and Related Disorders in [[Stockholm]], Sweden, 21 July (2002)
* Honorary member of the installation committee of the journal on [[Gender Identity Disorders]], the GID Journal (2003)
* Visiting professorship in sleep medicine (Amer.Ass.of Sleep Med.& Pfizer) at Stanford, CA, United States (2005-2006)
* Guest professor at the Beijing Institute of Radiation Medicine from 1 October 2005 to 31 December 2008 (2005-2008)
* Guest Professor at [[Zhejiang University]], [[Hangzhou]], [[China]] (2007)
* Academy medal for his role in national and international [[neuroscience]] (fundamental to applied), for his initiative to start the Netherlands Brain Bank, and for his research in Alzheimer's disease (2008)
* Honorary member of “Brein in Beeld” (2010)
* Chao Kuang Piu Chair of Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, P.R. China (2011–17)

===Key papers and publications===
Swaab has co-written extensively on a number of topics, including sexual [[Developmental biology|differentiation]] of the brain, Alzheimer's disease, [[Parkinson's disease]], [[Depression (mood)|depression]], [[eating disorders]] and [[metabolism]], [[multiple sclerosis]], human [[postmortem]] [[cell culture]], [[Huntington's disease]] and [[hypertension]].<ref name=CV />
